newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Stet sets sights on AT&T link.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Stet sets sights on AT&T link.

text.p: Italian government-owned telecommunications giant Stet is aiming to forge an alliance with AT&T Corp. by the end of the year, Stet Managing Director Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano said Wednesday.
Tommasi, talking to reporters at a meeting of Italian employers in Rome, said Stet was working intensively on reaching an accord with AT&T.
He gave no details, but asked when such an accord with the U.S. company might happen, he said: "The objective is to have an accord on an international alliance by the year-end."
Stet has been seeking a big international partner for months to turn it into a major player on the increasingly competitive world telecommunications stage.
It has a limited cooperation deal with International Business Machines Corp. and linked up earlier this year with AT&T to bid for the privatisation of Brazil's cellular phones.
Italian media have speculated the original AT&T partnership might lead to a bigger agreement, although up until now both companies have offered no comment.

The Italian company, which has a strong presence in South America, is looking to expand further and is bidding with Spain's Endesa for the privatisation of the country's Retevision as well as taking a 29 percent stake in Serbia Telekom.
The Rome government is eager to get a major international partnership in place before it privatises Stet, a move expected to take place next October after many delays.
